title: PS5 GPU Equivalent: PS5 and PS5 Pro PC Graphics Card Match
description: The PS5's 36-CU, 10.3 TFLOPS GPU roughly equals an RX 6700 or RTX 2070 Super. The 60-CU PS5 Pro lands near an RX 7700 XT, between an RTX 4060 Ti and 4070.
dek: The closest desktop graphics card and processor to the PS5 and PS5 Pro, worked out from Sony's published specs, with the PC parts that match or beat each one today.
quickAnswer: The PS5's GPU (36 RDNA 2 compute units at up to 2.23 GHz, about 10.3 TFLOPS) is roughly a desktop RX 6700 or RTX 2070 Super, and an RTX 4060, RTX 5060 or Arc B580 matches or slightly beats it. The PS5 Pro's 60-CU GPU, which Sony rates about 45 percent faster, lands roughly at an RX 7700 XT, between an RTX 4060 Ti and an RTX 4070.
intro: Sony published the key specs for both consoles. The PS5 has a custom AMD RDNA 2 GPU with 36 compute units at up to 2.23 GHz, 16 GB of GDDR6 shared with the CPU at 448 GB/s, and an 8-core Zen 2 CPU at up to 3.5 GHz. The PS5 Pro raises the GPU to 60 compute units, with memory Sony rates 28 percent faster and rendering it rates up to 45 percent faster. This page matches both to the desktop GPU and CPU that perform most like them.

These are rough, widely reported equivalents, built from the published specs and from how the closest desktop RDNA 2 and RDNA 3 cards perform in independent reviews. We have not tested either console. Console games are tuned for one fixed GPU, so a well-made port can beat a PC card that looks faster on paper, and a poor one can fall short.

sections.h: How We Matched the PS5 to Desktop Parts
body: The PS5's GPU uses AMD's RDNA 2 architecture, the same design as the Radeon RX 6000 series, so the cleanest comparison is the desktop card with the same number of compute units. That card is the RX 6700, the 10 GB model, which also has 36 RDNA 2 compute units. It runs at a higher boost clock and adds an Infinity Cache the PS5 lacks, but has a narrower 160-bit memory bus at 320 GB/s against the PS5's 256-bit bus at 448 GB/s. On paper the two land close together, which is why the RX 6700 is the match most comparisons settle on.

On the NVIDIA side, the widely reported match is an RTX 2070 Super, which also has 448 GB/s of memory bandwidth. Side-by-side tests of the same games on PS5 and PC, such as those published by Digital Foundry, generally place the PS5 around a 2070 Super, sometimes reaching RTX 2080 level in a well-optimized port. Roughly means within about 10 percent on average.

The CPU is the easy part. The PS5's 8-core, 16-thread Zen 2 chip runs at up to 3.5 GHz with less cache than desktop Zen 2, so in games it lands near a Ryzen 5 3600 or a Ryzen 7 3700X held to lower clocks. Any current desktop CPU is much faster.

sections.h: What Is the PS5 GPU Equivalent?
body: The PS5 GPU's closest desktop equivalent is an AMD Radeon RX 6700, the 10 GB card that shares its 36 RDNA 2 compute units. In NVIDIA terms it is roughly an RTX 2070 Super. That is the card to picture when you read 10.3 TFLOPS: comfortable at 1080p and 1440p with upscaling, and reliant on dynamic resolution or upscaling for the 4K output most PS5 games advertise.

In today's lineup, an [RTX 4060](/gear/rtx-4060/) or [Arc B580](/gear/arc-b580/) roughly matches or slightly beats a PS5 in raster, and the [RTX 5060](/gear/rtx-5060/) is a little faster again. All three add DLSS or XeSS, which usually look sharper than the upscaling most PS5 games use. The [RX 6600](/gear/rx-6600/) is somewhat slower than a PS5, and the [RX 6700 XT](/gear/rx-6700-xt/) a little faster.

The 2070 Super comparison has one catch: that card has 8 GB of VRAM, and so does the RTX 4060. The PS5 gives games roughly 12 to 13.5 GB of its 16 GB pool, so ports built around it can ask for more than 8 GB of video memory at high textures.

sections.h: What Is the PS5 Pro GPU Equivalent?
body: The PS5 Pro GPU's closest desktop equivalent is roughly an RX 7700 XT, or between an RTX 4060 Ti and an RTX 4070 on the NVIDIA side. Sony's own figure is that the Pro renders up to 45 percent faster than the PS5. Applied to a PS5 that sits near an RX 6700, that lands in RX 7700 XT territory, and independent side-by-side tests broadly agree.

On paper the Pro has 60 compute units, the same count as a desktop RX 6800, but it runs them at lower clocks within a console power budget, so the unit count overstates it. Sony rates its memory bandwidth 28 percent higher than the PS5's 448 GB/s, and it adds 2 GB of DDR5 for system tasks, which frees more of the 16 GB GDDR6 pool for games.

Ray tracing improved more than raster. Sony quotes two to three times the PS5's ray tracing speed in some cases, which narrows the gap to NVIDIA but does not close it: an [RTX 5070](/gear/rtx-5070/) still leads clearly with heavy RT. The Pro also adds PSSR, Sony's machine-learning upscaler, which plays the same role as DLSS or FSR 4.

sections.h: What Is the PS5 GPU Equivalent in NVIDIA?
body: The PS5 GPU's NVIDIA equivalent is roughly an RTX 2070 Super, sometimes an RTX 2080 in well-optimized ports. In current cards, the RTX 4060 is about even in raster and the RTX 5060 a little faster. For the PS5 Pro, the NVIDIA match is between an RTX 4060 Ti and an [RTX 4070](/gear/rtx-4070/), about where the [RTX 5060 Ti 16GB](/gear/rtx-5060-ti-16gb/) sits today.

With ray tracing on, the PS5 drops closer to an RTX 2060 Super or RTX 3060, because its RDNA 2 graphics have the same limited ray-tracing hardware as the RX 6000 series. DLSS widens the gap further: at the same internal resolution, DLSS usually gives a sharper image than the upscaling most PS5 games use.

sections.h: Is the PS5 Pro Worth It Over a PC Graphics Card?
body: It depends on what you already own. If you have a PC with a recent 6-core or 8-core CPU, a 16 GB card such as the [RX 9060 XT 16GB](/gear/rx-9060-xt-16gb/) or [RTX 5060 Ti 16GB](/gear/rtx-5060-ti-16gb/) gets you to PS5 Pro class raster for less than the console, with more VRAM for games to use and an upscaler that is as good or better. An RTX 5070 or [RX 9070](/gear/rx-9070/) clearly beats it.

If you are starting from nothing, a whole PC at PS5 Pro level costs more than the console once you add a CPU, motherboard, memory, storage, power supply, case and Windows. DRAM and SSD prices have swung hard since late 2025, which widens that gap. The console's advantages are price for the whole box, a fixed target that developers tune for, and Sony's exclusives on day one.

sections.h: What Is the PS5 CPU Equivalent?
body: The PS5 CPU is an 8-core, 16-thread AMD Zen 2 design at up to 3.5 GHz, with a smaller L3 cache than desktop Zen 2. It performs roughly like a Ryzen 7 3700X held to lower clocks, or a Ryzen 7 4700G; in games it lands closer to a Ryzen 5 3600. In Intel terms, that is roughly a Core i5-10400F to i7-10700 for gaming.

The PS5 Pro keeps the same 8-core Zen 2 design at up to 3.85 GHz, a small step up, so its CPU equivalent is the same class. That is why some games run at the same frame rate target on both consoles: the Pro's extra power goes to resolution and image quality, not to CPU-limited frame rates.

Any current desktop CPU is much faster. A [Ryzen 5 7600](/gear/ryzen-5-7600/) or [Ryzen 7 5700X3D](/gear/ryzen-7-5700x3d/) comfortably beats both consoles' CPUs. Check any CPU and GPU pairing with the [bottleneck calculator](/tools/bottleneck-calculator/).

sections.h: PS5 vs Xbox Series X vs Steam Machine: Which GPU Is Fastest?
body: Among standard consoles, the PS5 and Xbox Series X are close. The Series X has more compute units (52) at a lower clock, about 12.1 TFLOPS against the PS5's 10.3, and performs roughly like an RTX 2080; the PS5's higher clock lets it match or win in some games. See [Xbox Series X GPU equivalent](/xbox-series-x-gpu-equivalent/) for that breakdown.

Valve's Steam Machine has a newer RDNA 3 GPU but only 28 compute units, and lands roughly at an RX 6600 XT, a step below the PS5 in GPU power but well ahead in CPU power. The [Steam Machine GPU equivalent](/steam-machine-gpu-equivalent/) page covers it. The PS5 Pro is the fastest of the four in graphics.

sections.h: What PC Matches a PS5 or PS5 Pro?
body: A PC that matches or slightly beats a PS5 in most games needs a GPU at RTX 4060 level or better, a 6-core CPU from the last few years, and 16 GB of system RAM. With new parts, that means an RTX 5060 or Arc B580 with a Ryzen 5 7600. For PS5 ports with heavy textures, the 12 GB B580 or a 16 GB card is the safer pick than an 8 GB one. See [RTX 5060 vs Arc B580](/compare/rtx-5060-vs-arc-b580/) for that trade-off.

To match a PS5 Pro, step up to an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB or RX 9060 XT 16GB; to clearly beat it, an RTX 5070 or RX 9070. The [best budget graphics cards](/best-budget-graphics-card/) list ranks the cheaper options by price. Street prices below are USD bands and move week to week.

mistakes: 10.3 TFLOPS on RDNA 2 does not equal 10.3 TFLOPS on an NVIDIA or RDNA 3 card. Newer designs count throughput differently, so use the RDNA 2 cards with the same compute units, then performance tests, to match the PS5.
Matching the PS5 with an 8 GB card for big ports
PS5 games can use roughly 12 to 13.5 GB of memory. On PC, ports built for that pool ask for more than 8 GB of VRAM at high textures, so a 12 GB or 16 GB card matches the PS5 experience more reliably.
Most PS5 games reach 4K output with dynamic resolution or upscaling. Compare a PS5 to desktop cards at 1440p with upscaling, not native 4K results.
Assuming the PS5 Pro has a faster CPU
The Pro keeps the same 8-core Zen 2 CPU at a slightly higher clock. Its gains are in graphics, so CPU-limited games run at much the same frame rate as on a base PS5.
bottomLine: The PS5's GPU, 36 RDNA 2 compute units at up to 2.23 GHz and about 10.3 TFLOPS, is roughly a desktop RX 6700 or RTX 2070 Super, and an RTX 4060, RTX 5060 or Arc B580 matches or slightly beats it today. The PS5 Pro's 60-CU GPU, rated about 45 percent faster by Sony, lands near an RX 7700 XT, between an RTX 4060 Ti and an RTX 4070. Both consoles' Zen 2 CPUs sit near a Ryzen 5 3600 in games. For PC builds, prefer 12 GB or more of VRAM to match the PS5's memory pool.

faqs.q: What GPU is the PS5 equivalent to?
faqs.a: Roughly a desktop RX 6700 or RTX 2070 Super. The PS5 has 36 RDNA 2 compute units at up to 2.23 GHz, about 10.3 TFLOPS, the same unit count as the RX 6700. Current cards that match or slightly beat it include the RTX 4060, RTX 5060 and Arc B580.

faqs.q: What GPU is the PS5 Pro equivalent to?
faqs.a: Roughly an RX 7700 XT, or between an RTX 4060 Ti and an RTX 4070. Sony rates the Pro's 60-CU GPU up to 45 percent faster than the PS5 in rendering, with 28 percent more memory bandwidth.

faqs.q: What is the PS5 GPU equivalent in NVIDIA?
faqs.a: An RTX 2070 Super in raster, sometimes reaching RTX 2080 level in well-optimized ports. With ray tracing on, it falls closer to an RTX 2060 Super or RTX 3060. Today, the RTX 4060 is about even and the RTX 5060 a little faster.

faqs.q: Is an RTX 4060 better than a PS5?
faqs.a: Roughly even in raster, ahead with ray tracing and DLSS. Its weak spot is 8 GB of VRAM: PS5 ports with heavy textures can need more, where the PS5's shared 16 GB pool gives games roughly 12 to 13.5 GB.

faqs.q: How many TFLOPS is the PS5?
faqs.a: About 10.3 TFLOPS, from 36 RDNA 2 compute units at up to 2.23 GHz. The Xbox Series X is about 12.1 TFLOPS. TFLOPS only compare fairly within the same architecture, so use them alongside game tests.

faqs.q: What CPU is the PS5 equivalent to?
faqs.a: A Ryzen 7 3700X held to lower clocks, landing closer to a Ryzen 5 3600 in games: 8 Zen 2 cores at up to 3.5 GHz with less cache. The PS5 Pro runs the same design at up to 3.85 GHz.

faqs.q: Is the PS5 more powerful than the Steam Machine?
faqs.a: In GPU power, probably yes: the PS5 sits near an RX 6700, the Steam Machine near an RX 6600 XT by its specs. The Steam Machine's 6-core Zen 4 CPU is much faster than the PS5's Zen 2 chip.

faqs.q: What graphics card do I need to match a PS5 Pro?
faqs.a: A 16 GB card such as the RX 9060 XT 16GB or RTX 5060 Ti 16GB lands at PS5 Pro class raster, and an RTX 5070 or RX 9070 clearly beats it. Pair it with a recent 6-core CPU such as a Ryzen 5 7600.
